issues.issue_title: [Bug]:   SUCCESS is set before LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate executes and before BRR validation — function can return SUCCESS with an invalid BRR
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: [Bug]: SUCCESS is set before LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate executes and before BRR validation — function can return SUCCESS with an invalid BRR
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=UART, layer=LL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=18
Root cause: Hello @egtduncanbarclay, Thank you for the report.
Fix: ### Bug Summary bad code ### Detailed Description File: stm32g0xx_ll_lpuart.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: LL, UART, bug_report, medium, bug, invalid, hal, lpuart, SUCCESS, LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate, BRR, assert_param

Technical details:
### Bug Summary bad code ### Detailed Description File: stm32g0xx_ll_lpuart.c (and stm32g0xx_ll_usart.c — same pattern) • Issue 1: status = SUCCESS is set before LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate executes and before BRR validation — function can return SUCCESS with an invalid BRR • Issue 2: BRR range checks use assert_param which is a no-op without USE_FULL_ASSERT, so there is no runtime validation in production builds • Issue 3: On the error path (bad clock/baudrate), CR1/CR2/CR3/PRESC are already written, leaving the peripheral half-configured ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Actual Behavior _No response_ ### Environment _No response_ ### Severity Normal

Key comments:
Hello @egtduncanbarclay, Thank you for the report. Regarding the issues, the status variable in **LL_LPUART_Init()** is not intended to validate the BRR. Its role is simply to indicate whether LL_LPUART_Init() was able to initialize the LPUART registers according to the parameters provided in **LPUART_InitTypeDef**. Also, **LL_LPUART_SetBaudRate()** is implemented as a **__STATIC_INLINE** function. By design, it is used to perform small register-level operations efficiently with minimal call overhead. If you need BRR checking, you should enable USE_FULL_ASSERT and implement your own assert_failed() handler so that any invalid parameter can be handled in a way that matches your application requirements. This is consistent with the LL approach, which prioritizes lightweight direct register access and minimal overhead. In comparison, the HAL layer provides more built-in checks and a higher level of abstraction. Hello @egtduncanbarclay, Please allow me to close the issue. Thank you for your understanding.

Problem: [Question]: HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop stops complete htim instance
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=17
Root cause: Hello @JRStolle, Thank you for your report, This behavior is intentional.
Fix: ### Question Summary Why does HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop stop the complete timer peripheral ### Detailed Description In the HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop in the file stm32g0xx_hal_tim.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, usage_question, medium, question, tim, HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop, Macro__HAL_TIM_DISABLE

Technical details:
### Question Summary Why does HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop stop the complete timer peripheral ### Detailed Description In the HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop in the file stm32g0xx_hal_tim.c (version 1.6.3) the Macro__HAL_TIM_DISABLE(htim); is called. This is a bit confusing, since I would expect only the specific Channel from the functions arguments to be disabled. Is this the intended behaviour?

Key comments:
Hello @JRStolle, Thank you for your report, This behavior is intentional. HAL_TIM_PWM_Stop first disables only the requested PWM channel, then calls __HAL_TIM_DISABLE. However, __HAL_TIM_DISABLE disables the timer counter only if all CCx/CCxN channels are already disabled. Therefore: - If other channels on the same timer are still active, the timer keeps running. - If you stop the last active channel, the timer is stopped. Thank you for your reply. Yes, I did not look inside the Makro, since the description said that it disables the TIM peripheral. So if I want to disable the peripheral I have to make sure, to disable all channels first. This might be good idea to put into the description. Thanks!

issues.issue_title: LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() does not respect the reserved bits
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() does not respect the reserved bits
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=LL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=12
Root cause: Hello again @rdiez, Regarding this issue, LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() does not overwrite all bits.
Fix: All TIMx status registers documented in RM0444 have some bits which state "Reserved, must be kept at reset value".
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: LL, bug_report, low, bug, wontfix, hal, tim, RM0444, MODIFY_REG, LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE

Technical details:
All TIMx status registers documented in RM0444 have some bits which state "Reserved, must be kept at reset value". You then normally read the register, modify the bits you are interested in, and then write the new value. Usually, this is done with MODIFY_REG. This is done for compatibility reasons, in case some newer microcontroller has more flags at the reserved bits. However, LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() overwrites all bits. I would at least write a comment in LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() stating whether that could be a problem.

Key comments:
Hello again @rdiez, Regarding this issue, LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() does not overwrite all bits. If you look at any TIMx_SR register in the RM0444, you will see the abbreviation rc_w0 (see page 55 of the RM0444): **read/clear write0 (rc_w0) Software can read as well as clear this bit by writing 0. Writing 1 has no effect on the bit value** Since writing 1 has no effect. That's why we have WRITE_REG(TIMx->SR, ~(TIM_SR_UIF)); inside LL_TIM_ClearFlag_UPDATE() Karim In understand now, thanks. But shouldn't the reserved bits be documented as "rc_w0" then? At the moment, the documentation only states "Reserved, must be kept at reset value". Given that the reset value is documented as 0, but writing a 0 would clear the bit, then the documentation is misleading, isn't it? It should actually say that all reserved bits should be written with 1. Hello @rdiez, I have checked with our team, and it seems that for the sake of code flexibility (given the wide variety of timers), the Clear functions for the LL bits are always implemented in the same way, given that the reserved bits are neither significant nor impacted. It was a decision made by our development team. Thank you for your und

Problem: Possible unaligned memory access in `stm32g0xx_hal_spi.c`
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=10
Root cause: I just saw that this bug was also mentioned in https://github.
Fix: A bug in SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT() could lead to unaligned memory access, causing a hard fault.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, DMA, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, spi, SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT, MCU

Technical details:
A bug in SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT() could lead to unaligned memory access, causing a hard fault. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx-hal-driver/blob/11f6c302cf3caab45ea30c54b1120a47990704bd/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_spi.c#L3624 When hspi->TxXferCount is 2 or more and hspi->pTxBuffPtr points to a memory address which is not 16-bit-aligned, the MCU attempts a 16-bit access to the the named address. This leads to a hard fault through unaligned memory access, which is not possible on Cortex M0+: static void SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT(struct __SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi) { /* Transmit data in packing Bit mode */ if (hspi->TxXferCount >= 2U) { hspi->Instance->DR = *((uint16_t *)hspi->pTxBuffPtr); hspi->pTxBuffPtr += sizeof(uint16_t); hspi->TxXferCount -= 2U; } /* Transmit data in 8 Bit mode */ else { *(__IO uint8_t *)&hspi->Instance->DR = (*hspi->pTxBuffPtr); hspi->pTxBuffPtr++; hspi->TxXferCount--; } The bug have stayed undiscovered, as the code is working well as long as at least one of the following conditions is ensured: - Only one byte of data is read/written (else clause of the cited code is entered) - The source/destination data pointers are aligned to a 16-bit boundary by the linker - The code runs on a platform that tolerated unaligned access, for example Cortex M3 This could be fixed by completely removing the 16-bit-access in this function, as the function is per definition only called in 8-bit-mode: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx-hal-driver/blob/11f6c302cf3caab45ea30c54b1120a47990704bd/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_spi.c#L1831 A proposed solution: static void SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT(struct __SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi) { /* Transmit data in 8 Bit mode */ *(__IO uint8_t *)&hspi->Instance->DR = (*hspi->pTxBuffPtr); hspi->pTxBuffPtr++; hspi->TxXferCount--; The bug was reproduced by my with arm-gnu-toolchain-14.2.rel1-mingw-w64-x86_64-arm-none-eabi. It was also already mentioned in the ST forum several years ago: https://community.st.com/t5/stm32cubeide-mcus/pointers-and-hal-libs-gt-hardfault/td-p/286857 It could also be spotted by building the code wit -Wcast-align enabled.

Key comments:
I just saw that this bug was also mentioned in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx-hal-driver/issues/5 Unfortunately, the fix provided back then did not fix the root cause (16-bit-access when 8-bit-access is requested by the user). Hello @fgrie, Thank you for the report. As you mentioned, the bug relating to unaligned memory access was fixed by our Developpement team and explained in the brief section of the source file at the line 70. > Data buffer address alignment restriction: > (#) There is no support for unaligned accesses on the Cortex-M0 processor. > If the user wants to transfer in 16Bit data mode, it shall ensure that 16-bit aligned address is used for: > (##) pData parameter in HAL_SPI_Transmit(), HAL_SPI_Transmit_IT(), HAL_SPI_Receive() and HAL_SPI_Receive_IT() > (##) pTxData and pRxData parameters in HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive() and HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT() > (#) There is no such restriction when going through DMA by using HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA(), HAL_SPI_Receive_DMA() > and HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_DMA(). > however, regarding your proposal for the SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT() function, I will share it

issues.issue_title: HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback missing from STM32G0 HAL GPIO API
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback missing from STM32G0 HAL GPIO API
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F4XX, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=7
Root cause: Hello @insolace, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: Ali Labbene requested that I open a new issue here in this thread: https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F4XX, HAL, usage_question, high, enhancement, invalid, gpio, STM32G0, HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback, GPIO_Pin, HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Rising_Callback, HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Falling_Callback

Technical details:
Ali Labbene requested that I open a new issue here in this thread: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0/issues/7#issuecomment-2491193412 The STM32G0 HAL library does not include the standard HAL GPIO external interrupt callback. This is what we would expect: void HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback(uint16_t GPIO_Pin) { } Instead, STM32G0 only includes HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Rising_Callback() and HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Falling_Callback(). These functions are fine, but HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback is the standard API that is used with most (if not all) other STM32 HAL drivers, and if you google any "how to make an stm32 respond to GPIO" tutorial / walk through, HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback is the method that is shown. How To Reproduce: Compare stm32g0xx_hal_gpio.h in this repository to to https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f4xx-hal-driver/blob/master/Inc/stm32f4xx_hal_gpio.h and you will see the API method in question is missing in STM32G0.

Key comments:
Hello @insolace, Thank you for your contribution. This change is actually a new feature that enhances the functionality of the STM32G0 HAL library. By distinguishing between rising and falling edge interrupts. To implement this new feature, it was necessary to break compatibility with the previous single callback method. The reason for this is that there is a single entry point for the HAL GPIO interrupt service routine: HAL_GPIO_EXTI_IRQHandler(). It is not feasible to support both the legacy single callback method and the new dual callback method within this single entry point. As a result, you will need to adapt your code to align with the new implementation. By doing so, you will be able to take full advantage of the new hardware capabilities. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.

issues.issue_title: HAL I2C produces unwanted NACKs in slave mode
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL I2C produces unwanted NACKs in slave mode
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-G071RB, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=6
Root cause: Additional note: At least from my tests, the address byte cannot even be NACK'ed in the first place: Even with clock stretching & SBC enabled, the NACK bit is ignored when releasing the clock after the address byte.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * MCU: STM32G0B0RET **Describe the bug** It looks like the I2C HAL driver handles the NACK bit incorrectly, at least in slave mode with Slave Byte Control enabled.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-G071RB, HAL, bug_report, low, bug, invalid, i2c, MCU, STM32G0B0RET, NACK, STOP, ACK

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * MCU: STM32G0B0RET **Describe the bug** It looks like the I2C HAL driver handles the NACK bit incorrectly, at least in slave mode with Slave Byte Control enabled. Consider e.g. the following line: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/b3638742cfd2e8160f35f616f5ed19877e228f6e/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_i2c.c#L6291-L6292 This tries to "disable address acknowledge" after the current transaction has been completed. Similarly, the code tries to clear the bit in various places. From the documentation however, it is clear that this cannot work: > Bit 15 **NACK**: NACK generation (slave mode) The bit is set by software, cleared by hardware when the NACK is sent, or when a STOP condition or an Address matched is received, or when PE=0. 0: an ACK is sent after current received byte. 1: a NACK is sent after current received byte. _Note: Writing ‘0’ to this bit has no effect. This bit is used in slave mode only: in master receiver mode, NACK is automatically generated after last byte preceding STOP or RESTART condition, whatever the NACK bit value. When an overrun occurs in slave receiver NOSTRETCH mode, a NACK is automatically generated whatever the NACK bit value. When hardware PEC checking is enabled (PECBYTE=1), the PEC acknowledge value does not depend on the NACK value._ > > Source: RM0450, Page 762 (rm0454-stm32g0x0-advanced-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) Note the "Writing 0 to this bit has no effect". This means that once the bit is incorrectly set, it can never be fixed again **How To Reproduce** 1. Set up a board with the MCU, enable one of the I2C peripherals & hook up a device capable of being an I2C master 2. Add this code to the main file of a new project: c char buf; void start_receive(I2C_HandleTypeDef *hi2c) { LL_I2C_SetTransferSize(hi2c->Instance, 0); // set NBYTES to 0 to prevent premature release of clock LL_I2C_EnableReloadMode(hi2c->Instance); HAL_I2C_Slave_Seq_Receive_IT(hi2c, &buf, 1, I2C_FIRST_AND_NEXT_FRAME); LL_I2C_SetTransferSize(hi2c->Instance, 1); // set NBYTES to 1 to release clock & start receiving } void HAL_I2C_AddrCallback(I2C_HandleTypeDef *hi2c, uint8_t TransferDirection, uint16_t AddrMatchCode) { LL_I2C_EnableSlaveByteControl(hi2c->Instance); start_receive(hi2c); } void HAL_I2C_ListenCpltCallback(I2C_HandleTypeDef *hi2c) { HAL_I2C_EnableListen_IT(hi2c); } void HAL_I2C_SlaveRxCpltCallback(I2C_HandleTypeDef *hi2c) { start_receive(hi2c); } /* USER CODE END 0 */ /** * @brief The application entry point. * @retval int */ int main(void) { /* USER CODE BEGIN 1 */ /* USER CODE END 1 */ /* MCU Configuration--------------------------------------------------------*/ /* Reset of all peripherals, Initializes the Flash interface and the Systick. */ HAL_Init(); /* USER CODE BEGIN Init */ /* USER CODE END Init */ /* Configure the system clock */ SystemClock_Config(); /* USER CODE BEGIN SysInit */ /* USER CODE END SysInit */ /* Initialize all configured peripherals */ MX_GPIO_Init(); MX_I2C2_Init(); /* USER CODE BEGIN 2 */ HAL_I2C_EnableListen_IT(&hi2c2); /* USER CODE END 2 */ /* Infinite loop */ /* USER CODE BEGIN WHILE */ while (1) { /* USER CODE END WHILE */ /* USER CODE BEGIN 3 */ } /* USER CODE END 3 */ } 3. This code sets up the I2C slave to continuously receive bytes, e.g. ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52e37433-c0a4-4401-8e4b-838b21c3bc66) 4. Set a breakpoint in the following line: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/b3638742cfd2e8160f35f616f5ed19877e228f6e/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_i2c.c#L6291-L6292 5. Initiate two more I2C writes. The first will be acknowledged, then the breakpoint will be hit. 6. Continue execution. issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT crashes when TX buffer is not 16 bit aligned
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-G0B1RE, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=5
Root cause: ST internal Reference: 184492 Fixed in commit https://github.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * Tested on nucleo-g0b1re * arm-none-eabi-gcc version 10.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-G0B1RE, HAL, DMA, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, HAL_SPI_Receive_IT, HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT, MCU, SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * Tested on nucleo-g0b1re * arm-none-eabi-gcc version 10.3.1 (but compiler does not matter) **Describe the bug** Calling function HAL_SPI_Receive_IT() or HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_IT() with buffer not aligned to 16 bits crashes MCU **How To Reproduce** 1. Call HAL_SPI_Receive_IT() with unaligned buffer and more then 1 byte to send **Additional context** Real problem however is in SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT() function that tries to optimize send using 16 bits access if there is more data. For **Cortex-M0+** unaligned read results in fault. c static void SPI_2linesTxISR_8BIT(struct __SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi) { /* Transmit data in packing Bit mode */ if (hspi->TxXferCount >= 2U && ((uint32_t)(hspi->pTxBuffPtr) & 1) == 0) // <= !!!! Additional check to use 8 bit for unaligned buffer here fixes the problem { hspi->Instance->DR = *((uint16_t *)hspi->pTxBuffPtr); // <= !!! Crashes here on Cortex-M0+ hspi->pTxBuffPtr += sizeof(uint16_t); hspi->TxXferCount -= 2U; } ...

Key comments:
ST internal Reference: 184492 Fixed in commit https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/commit/1c95709a51b5a32e02c1469e12e5cfe6b8a1ce71 It's hard do believe that simple bug (unnecessary optimization that was flawed and could be fixed in one line) resulted in change of API that is less functional than before, adds a lot of checks that are not really needed. It's not that SPI hardware has some limitation that restrict buffer alignment it's just unreasonable approach that uses "optimization". Now if one uses DMA API that works fine and for some reason wants to switch to IT that has similar API and could be used interchangeable user can face serious crash and go through debugging to find out that both API are not compatible and application has to be aware of this unnecessary limitation (that is not present in non-Cortex-M0 based MCU's). This is very disappointing solution and hardly could be referred as fixed but if counts toward KPI.

issues.issue_title: Timeout parameter in HAL_I2C_Master_Receive/HAL_I2C_Mem_Read not used for I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout function
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Timeout parameter in HAL_I2C_Master_Receive/HAL_I2C_Mem_Read not used for I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout function
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=4
Root cause: Hello @Kedrel, Thank you for the report.
Fix: Hello, I found that the Timeout parameter in both HAL_I2C_Master_Receive & HAL_I2C_Mem_Read functions is not used in these two lines: https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, usage_question, high, question, i2c, HAL_I2C_Master_Receive, HAL_I2C_Mem_Read, SET, HAL_OK

Technical details:
Hello, I found that the Timeout parameter in both HAL_I2C_Master_Receive & HAL_I2C_Mem_Read functions is not used in these two lines: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/dabe885cefd3c201c1d8aa1cc98657db7b76a309/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_i2c.c#L1273 https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/dabe885cefd3c201c1d8aa1cc98657db7b76a309/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_i2c.c#L2670 I'm not sure if this is a bug, but in my case, I need to change it to : _if (I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout(hi2c, I2C_FLAG_BUSY, SET, Timeout, tickstart) != HAL_OK)_ **How to reproduce the "bug "**: Call the HAL_I2C_Master_Receive or HAL_I2C_Mem_Read function with a timeout parameter of less than 25ms, and don't power up the i2c device to trigger the timeout.

Key comments:
Hello @Kedrel, Thank you for the report. The Timeout used in I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout for the 2 functions HAL_I2C_Master_Receive & HAL_I2C_Mem_Read is sufficient to check if the peripheral still busy. Otherwise, can you share more details about your scenario or project? With regards. Hello @KRASTM, The system i'm working on currently uses a tick of 10 ms to run the whole process. The aim is never to have a task that exceends 10ms so we can handle the "real-time" properly. When i call "**HAL_I2C_Mem_Read**" using a Timeout parameter at 2 ms, inside of it we have the call of "**I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout**" which uses a parameter of **I2C_TIMEOUT_BUSY**, which is 25ms. So if an I2C peripheral can't respond, instead of loosing 2ms of wait time like the setting i chose, i'll loose 25ms. I can't afford to loose 25ms like that (as i have multiple I2C sensors), so i'll change the **I2C_TIMEOUT_BUSY** value to something acceptable for my application. With regards. Hello @Kedrel, In this particular case, it is possible to modify the value of I2C_TIMEOUT_BUSY to suit your application. Please allow me to close this issue. Thank you for your comprehension. With regards.

issues.issue_title: USB OUT stall's on high bus load
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: USB OUT stall's on high bus load
Context: repo=stm32g0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-G0B1RE, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=2
Root cause: Hi @lichtfeind, Please excuse this delayed reply.
Fix: I have a firmware running on the NUCLEO-G0B1RE that receives bulk out transfers over USB and echos them back.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-G0B1RE, HAL, USB, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, STALL, candleLight_fw, BLSIZE, NUM_BLOCK, COUNTn_RX

Technical details:
I have a firmware running on the NUCLEO-G0B1RE that receives bulk out transfers over USB and echos them back. The endpoint is setup for double buffering. At high bus load some transfers are aborted with a STALL. The firmware is ported by @marckleinebudde can be found here https://github.com/marckleinebudde/candleLight_fw/tree/stm32g0 I suspect the cause to be in [Inc/stm32g0xx_ll_usb.h#L659](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx_hal_driver/blob/master/Inc/stm32g0xx_ll_usb.h#L659). It does two writes to the buffer descriptor table. One to clear BLSIZE, NUM_BLOCK and COUNTn_RX and one the set BLSIZE and NUM_BLOCK. This results in a small window in which NUM_BLOCK is 0 while the endpoint is valid. As stated in RM0444 37.5.2 > Reception memory buffer locations are written starting from the address contained in the > ADDRn_RX for a number of bytes corresponding to the received data packet length, or up > to the last allocated memory location, as defined by BLSIZE and NUM_BLOCK, whichever > comes first. In this way, the USB peripheral never writes beyond the end of the allocated > reception memory buffer area. If the length of the data packet payload (actual number of > bytes used by the application) is greater than the allocated buffer, the USB peripheral > detects a buffer overrun condition. In this case, a STALL handshake is sent instead of the > usual ACK to notify the problem to the host, no interrupt is generated and the transaction is > considered failed. So either make sure COUNTn_RX is cleared without clearing NUM_BLOCK or setting STATRX to NAK while changing the entry.

Key comments:
